# Introduction
An interesting conclusion in any convex QRT on finite-dimensional state spaces, the generalized robustness can be interpreted operationally as the advantage of a quantum resource state in some channel discrimination task. 

We consider general QRTs on a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$.
The set $\mathcal{F} (\mathcal{H})$ of free states is defined as some closed subset of the density matrix $\mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})$ in the system $\mathcal{H}$. The generalized robustness resource quantifier is defined as follows.

:::{.callout-note icon="false"}
## Definition: Generalized Robustness

 Let $\rho \in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})$ be a quantum state. The generalized robustness $\mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F} (\mathcal{H})}(\rho)$ of $\rho$ with respect to the set $\mathcal{F} (\mathcal{H})$ of free states is defined as:
$$
 \mathcal{R}_{\mathcal{F} (\mathcal{H})}(\rho) = \min_{\tau \in \mathcal{D}(\mathcal{H})}  \left\{ s \geq 0 : \frac{\rho + s\tau}{1 + s} \in \mathcal{F} (\mathcal{H}) \right\}
$$
:::

:::{.callout-note icon="false"}
## Definition: Generalized Gell-Mann Matrices
For a $d$-dimensional Hilbert space $\mathcal{H}$ with the standard computational basis $\{|1\rangle, |2\rangle, \dots, |d\rangle\}$, the $d^2 - 1$ generalized Gell-Mann matrices are Hermitian operators defined by the following three categories:

1. Symmetric (off-diagonal) matrices: For $1 \le j < k \le d$,$\Lambda_S^{j,k} = |j\rangle\langle k| + |k\rangle\langle j|$
2. Antisymmetric (off-diagonal) matrices: For $1 \le j < k \le d$,$\Lambda_A^{j,k} = -i(|j\rangle\langle k| - |k\rangle\langle j|)$
3. Diagonal matrices: For $1 \le l \le d-1$,$\Lambda_D^{l} = \sqrt{\frac{2}{l(l+1)}} \left( \sum_{m=1}^{l} |m\rangle\langle m| - l|l+1\rangle\langle l+1| \right)$
:::

:::{#lem-orthon .callout-note icon="false"}
## (Orthogonality of Generalized Gell-Mann Matrices)
Let $\{\lambda_j\}$ denote the set of generalized Gell-Mann matrices defined above. For any two matrices $\lambda_i$ and $\lambda_j$ in this set, the trace inner product satisfies:$$\tr[\lambda_i^\dagger \lambda_j] = 2\delta_{ij}$$
:::
